drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 52-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.83, creatinine 0.97-1.24, hemoglobin 13.2-13.3, platelets 279-288, sodium 140-141, wbc 8.1-8.3; vitals dbp 67-71, heart_rate 81-87, map 86-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 121-127, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.51-1.78, hemoglobin 13.4, platelets 288-289, sodium 140-141, wbc 7.8-8.4; vitals dbp 67-70, heart_rate 81-85, map 86-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 122-128, spo2 95-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Hold lisinopril; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury ruled out. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 52-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury ruled out. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
